statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office — Company Name Reservation and Registration Portal (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in English or Māori; names in any other language must be transliterated into English alphabet characters; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name and must comply with the Companies Act 1993, ss 20–24; use of Māori words requires assessment of cultural appropriateness; trading names may be in additional languages but registered name must be in Latin script.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written objection to the Registrar of Companies within 20 working days of the rejection notice, citing the grounds under Companies Act ss 20–24; the Registrar must issue a formal decision; further appeal lies to the High Court of New Zealand under the Companies Act 1993 and Judicature Act provisions; alternatively, the applicant may file a new reservation with a different clarity suffix (e.g., 'Airline Inflight Catering Kitchen Limited' or 'Aviation Catering Services NZ Ltd'); ministerial approval from the relevant sector regulator (e.g., Ministry of Primary Industries for food-related terms or Civil Aviation Authority for aviation-related terms) may be required for sensitive tokens.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible: a registered office must be a physical address in New Zealand where legal notices may be served; virtual office provider that maintains a physical New Zealand street address and mail-forwarding service is acceptable for the registered office statutory address, but cannot serve as the actual inflight catering kitchen production location; the operational kitchen requires a separate fully compliant commercial food premises, and the registered office should not be represented as the principal place of business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (85%): Airport bonded catering kitchens are subject to unannounced inspections by New Zealand Food Safety (Ministry for Primary Industries), Civil Aviation Authority security audits, and airport authority health and safety compliance checks; expectation of annual physical inspection is near certain given ISIC 5621 scope classified as food production in a secure aviation environment.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), particularly ss 5-6 (definitions and company formation), ss 10-16 (incorporation), ss 20-32 (constitution and governance), ss 36-50 (share capital), s 128 (registered office), ss 152-161 (directors), and ss 360-368 (registration and remedial powers of the Registrar). Secondary legislation: the Companies (Share Capital) Regulations 2020 and the Companies (Postal and Electronic Communications) Regulations 1988. Incorporation is effected electronically under the Companies Act 1993 and the Electronic Transactions Act 2002 through the New Zealand Companies Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, part of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE); operational fililings are made through the Companies Office Online Portal located at Auckland and Wellington, accessible via www.companiesoffice.govt.nz.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation (online form on the Companies Office 'Incorporate Now' portal; historically also issued as Form N1), together with a constitution (optional but recommended), signed consents of directors and shareholders to act, and the required statement of registered office address and shareholding information.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital or escrow account requirement under New Zealand law. A company may be incorporated with one share of no par value, provided there is at least one shareholder and one director resident in New Zealand for the purpose of registered office service of documents. As a practical matter, the initial capital may be set at NZD 1.00 fully paid or a nominal issued share capital, with subsequent funding by subscription, shareholder loans, or retained earnings. No lodging of capital in an escrow account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CK_IC LIMITED (A COMPANY INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMPANIES ACT 1993; REGISTERED OFFICE IN NEW ZEALAND)

RESOLVED, at an authorised meeting of the board of directors, that:

1. Constitutional Adoption: The constitution filed at incorporation, as gazetted and approved by the sole incorporator, is adopted and ratified as the constitution of the company. The board shall ensure compliance with all constitutional provisions, including limitation of liability, distribution, and indemnity clauses.

2. Share Capital Subscription and Allotment: The initial subscribers (whether resident or non-resident, as permissible under the Companies Act 1993) having subscribed for shares in the company, the board approves the allotment and issuance of the proposed shares as set out in the incorporation application. Any consideration payable for the shares, whether in cash, kind, or by set-off against a shareholder loan, is accepted; share certificates shall be issued in accordance with the company's constitution and ss 80-96 of the Companies Act 1993.

3. Adoption of Registered Office: The registered office of the company within New Zealand at the stated place in the incorporation application is adopted under s 128. It is confirmed that the address is a physical location, not solely a post office box, and that the Registrar of Companies has been notified accordingly.

4. Appointment of Directors and Officers: The persons named in the incorporation application as directors are elected and employed as directors under s 152, with the following offices: [name] as Managing Director, [name] as Chief Financial Officer, and [name] as Compliance Officer for licensing and food safety matters. Any requisite 'consent to act' forms having been signed, the directors are authorised to manage the business and exercise the board powers provided in the Companies Act 1993 and the constitution.

5. Appointment of Company Officer and GovernanceIR: Pending no statutory requirement for a company secretary, the board, where desired, appoints a company officer responsible for statutory registers, share registry, and compliance filings with the Companies Office and the New Zealand Inland Revenue Department.

6. Banking Authorisation: The managing director and chief financial officer are jointly authorised to open, maintain, and operate bank accounts in the name of CK_IC Limited, to sign cheques and electronic payment instructions, and to receive merger and aviation contract wire transfers and monthly ACH payments, subject to mandatory dual authorisation for amounts exceeding NZD 25,000.

7. Establishment of Catering Undertaking: Subject to all industrial and environmental licences being issued, the board approves the undertaking of airline inflight catering, fine-dining catering, and airport direct ramp delivery services as an ISIC 5621 activity. The compliance officer is instructed to procure food registration, environmental permits, and airport security clearances before operational commencement.

8. Regulatory Filing: The board authorises the preparation and filing of all necessary annual returns, filings with the Companies Registrar, registration with Inland Revenue for goods and services tax (GST) and PAYE where applicable, and any such applications as the board determines in accordance with the statute and constitution.

9. Indemnification and Insurance: The board approves the procurement of directors' and officers' liability insurance, public and products liability cover, and property insurance for the food kitchen and ramp vehicles.

The resolution was passed unanimously and recorded in the minute book on the day of incorporation.

Signed: _________________________________ (Chair)   Date: _________________________________

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-Incorporation Structure and Governance Design Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private legal counsel / New Zealand Companies Office advisory desk (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate structure to ensure that CK_IC Limited's membership, directors, registered office, and share classes conform to the Companies Act 1993 and the targeted customer's cross-border gatekeeper obligations. Draft or adopt a constitution: either the Companies Act default rules or a custom constitution covering pre-emptive sale of shares, distributions, director-restricted powers, and explicit consent to INZ-owned foreign shareholding. Ensure at least one individual director is resident in New Zealand as required by s 152(2). Collect identity documents, CVs, proof of physical address for each director and shareholder, and signed consents to act. This step creates the underlying dossier for the electronic incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of all directors and shareholders
Proof of residential address within the last three months (utility bill or bank statement)
Proposed constitution (if customising default rules)
Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
Signed share subscription agreement for the initial shares
Written confirmation of the registered office address within New Zealand
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the consent forms are incomplete or the registered office is a PO Box, counsel will immediately procure corrected documentation and re-file. If doubt exists regarding name suitability or share class taxation, an interpretive advice request can be submitted to the Companies Office Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Search and Reservation (Optional Non-Mandatory Step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Online Name Reservation Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online search in the New Zealand Companies Register and New Zealand Intellectual Property trademark database for the intended name 'CK_IC Limited' or any desired trading name (e.g. 'Airline Inflight Catering Kitchen'). Reserve the name via the Companies Office 'Apply for Name' online service if the company is to use a distinct legal name that is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company. The name reservation is available for 20 working days and is not needed if the exact company name is accepted at incorporation, but is recommended to avoid rejection.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal company name
Reference to the intended ISIC 5621 business scope statement
Relevant search results from the Companies Register
If a restricted word is used, the required Ministerial approval or professional licence endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any name search flags a conflict, the applicant may file a contention letter or manually modify the name with a descriptive suffix (e.g. 'CK Inflight Catering (NZ) Limited'). If a desired name has been otherwise used, the registrant can apply to the Registrar for approval in cases of honest concurrent use, or alternatively adopt a distinctive secondary name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Incorporation Filing with the Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies / New Zealand Companies Office Online Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online 'Incorporate Now' application to the Registrar. The applicant must provide the company's legal name, registered office physical address, director details (including residential address and birth date), shareholder details, share allocation, and any adopted constitution. The constitution must be uploaded as a PDF appended to the application. If the company intends to contract with airport operators and to receive aviation contract wire transfers, the constitution should state that the primary business is inflight catering services and that the company may acquire and hold airport airside permits. After filing, the Registrar performs a statutory validation of the application against the Companies Act 1993 and publicly registers the company. A fee is payable online; approval is usually granted almost immediately on the same working day.
required_dossiers: Online incorporation application (Form N1 equivalent)
Constitution (as adopted and signed)
Director consents to act
Shareholder consents and share subscription forms
Notice of registered office address
Payment of the Companies Office registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the Registrar issues a notice to the applicant stating the deficiency under s 360 of the Companies Act. The applicant has 10 working days (or the extended period permitted by the Registrar) to submit corrected documents via the online portal or make a written demonstration. Should the Registrar refuse registration, the applicant may apply to the High Court for judicial review. In practice, the Companies Office proactively identifies missing consents or address anomalies, allowing immediate electronic correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and New Zealand Business Number (NZBN)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / New Zealand Business Number Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Registrar issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation under s 15 of the Companies Act. The certificate contains the registered company number and is automatically entered into the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register. The company obtains an NZBN, which serves as the unique business identifier for all government and private-sector transactions. This certificate authorises the company to commence legal existence but does not yet authorise food manufacture; operational licences are addressed in the next stages.
required_dossiers: Accepted incorporation application
Confirmation of company name and registered office
No additional dossier beyond the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or NZBN is delayed, the applicant may contact the NZBN customer help service or Companies Office to request a verification copy. If any detail on the certificate is inaccurate, the company may file an amendment with the Companies Office under s 24 and, where necessary, apply to the Registrar for reissue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Registers and Corporate Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors / New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after incorporation, the board shall record the First Board Resolution in the minute book, issue share certificates, and open the statutory registers as required by subparts 4 and 5 of the Companies Act 1993. The registers must capture: shareholders and share transfers; directors and their consents; charges over the company assets appointed to any lender; the location of the registered office; and the company's principal place of business. If a managing director, CFO, or compliance officer is appointed, their appointment must be recorded in the register of directors and served upon the Registrar as a change of registered details, along with a return stating any officeholders.
required_dossiers: Minute book containing the First Board Resolution
Share certificates and share register
Directors' and officeholders' registers
Registered office confirmation
Certificate of Incorporation
Director consent forms and share subscription agreements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If there is an inconsistency between the statutory register and the application record, the board must file a 'Notice of Change of Particulars' with the Companies Office within 10 working days. If the issue concerns the allotment of shares or any variation of class rights, the board can adopt a corrective resolution; in contested circumstances, an application may be made to the High Court for relief under s 174.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registrations with Inland Revenue and Customs-Related Account Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) / New Zealand Customs Service if importing bonded inputs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, register the company with IRD for IRD number, GST, PAYE and resident withholding tax. For GST, registration is mandatory once annual turnover exceeds NZD 60,000 or if the company opts to register voluntarily; most commercial inflight caterers register from day one to claim input credits on equipment and raw materials. If the kitchen will receive goods entering a customs-controlled airport area, the company should apply for a New Zealand Customs trader identification and any relevant deferred or bonded duty facility for handling air miles international supplies. Additionally, if the entity makes aviation contract wire remittances abroad, advise the MTM mailbox for dividend or royalty remittances to be tax-compliant under the Income Tax Act 2007.
required_dossiers: Company Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Bank account confirmation
Registered office and principal place of business details
Business address and contact person details
Expected annual turnover (for GST boundary determination)
If required, Customs registration for bonded catering stores
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: IRD notices of unacceptable application are generally due to missing proof of physical address or bank verification. Correct the application through the IRD myIR portal within 5 working days. For GST or PAYE disputes, the company may seek a statutory tax ruling or file an objection with IRD as prescribed by the Tax Administration Act 1994.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Compliance Blueprint for the Airline Catering Physical and Environmental Licenses
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (New Zealand Food Safety), New Zealand Civil Aviation Authority, local territorial authority, and regional council
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Commence the application for the food safety registration and the environmental and airport-related authorisations in parallel with formation. The company must identify the territorial authority where the kitchen will operate and either attest that it operates under a National Programme or implement a Food Control Plan (FCP) under the Food Act 2014. Prepare the pre-requisite programs, hazard analysis, and HACCP-based group docs to submit with the Food Control Plan registration. For any discharge of cooking grease, wastewater and odour, submit an application to the relevant regional council for trade waste permits and discharge consents under the Resource Management Act 1991. Should the facility be located within any airport aerodrome buffer, obtain airside security clearances from the airport operator and the Civil Aviation Authority, including all personnel background vetting.
required_dossiers: Food Control Plan / Food Safety Program (under Food Act 2014)
Site floor plan and sanitisation schedule
Wastewater and grease trap design
Ventilation and odour control system diagrams
Proposed waste disposal and cleaning contracts
Employees' identification and security vetting forms for airside access
Heating, ventilation and air conditioning system details for building compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the local council or MPI refuses the registration, the company may file for re-assessment under the Food Act 2014 food registration appeals process, and may escalate to administrative review by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade if unfair trade issues arise. For resource consent refusal, an appeal lies to the Environment Court under s 120 of the Resource Management Act 1991. For any aviation safety rejection, the applicant may seek a review under the Civil Aviation Act 1990 before contesting the decision in the District Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) – New Zealand Food Safety, local territorial authority environmental health department, and the Civil Aviation Authority of New Zealand (CAA). For airports on land subject to the Resource Management Act 1991, the relevant regional council (e.g. Auckland Council, Christchurch City Council, or Wellington Regional Council) also acts as licensing authority for discharge and trade waste permits. The airport aerodrome operator issues the airside security and operational clearance to the catering kitchen.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Act 2014 Registration (Food Control Plan or National Programme) issued by the territorial authority / MPI; if applicable, a National Environmental Consent or Regional Resource Consent for the discharge of cooking-related wastewater, airborne emissions, and trade waste; and an Airport Airside Security and Vehicle Mobility Permit issued by the aerodrome operator and CAA.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) with delegation to regional councils for site-specific assessments; for airport sites the relevant regional council exercises consent authority for discharge permits under the Resource Management Act 1991.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: The facility is generally classified as a low-to-moderate environmental impact activity, requiring a 'Controlled Activity' or 'Permitted Activity' assessment. A full 'Assessment of Environmental Effects (AEE)' is not automatically mandated for an inflight catering kitchen; however, if the planned gross floor area exceeds local district plan thresholds, or if the site discharges to water, odour, or airborne particulate all above permissive standards, a resource consent application accompanied by an AEE under Schedule 4 of the Resource Management Act 1991 will be required. For a large-scale industrial scale kitchen serving multiple airlines, the responsible regional council may require a full AEE incorporating air dispersion modelling and noise assessments.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance must be met with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ 2004) and the National Environmental Standards for Sources of Human Drinking Water. For trade waste discharges, the kitchen must observe the local authority Trade Waste Bylaw: incoming wastewaters shall not contain pH outside 6.0-11.0, BOD loading exceeding the agreed consent level (typically 250-300 mg/L), total suspended solids exceeding 300 mg/L, fats, oils and grease (FOG) above 50 mg/L, and temperature above 60°C at the boundary of the fat trap. Kitchen exhaust emissions from cooking oil vapours, particulates, odour, and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) must be treated with certified grease extraction systems and, if required by the district plan, an air-discharge licence setting odour limits (commonly a 1-in-50 diluent standard at the property boundary). Waste solids must be segregated, oils collected by licensed waste carrier, and all hazardous chemicals stored and used in accordance with WorkSafe hazardous substances regulations. Where the site is within an airport protected aerodrome area, lighting and engine test emissions are additionally regulated by the CAA and local plan rules.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Under the Building Act 2004, the catering kitchen must obtain a Building Consent and a Code Compliance Certificate (or, for new use of an existing building, a building warrant of fitness) covering structural, sanitary, fire, and mechanical ventilation compliance. The facility must secure a Fire Safety Evacuation Plan approved by Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ), including commercial kitchen fire suppression systems, grease-duct fire protection, extinguishers, and clear evacuation signage. Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, a Workplace Health and Safety audit must be completed, and, where hazardous substances (e.g. ammonia cooling systems, industrial cleaning agents, propane cylinders) are present, an additional 'Hazardous Substances and New Organisms (HSNO) Test Certificate' from WorkSafe New Zealand is mandatory. For personnel accessing secure airside areas of an airport, background checks, identity verification and a Civil Aviation Authority security clearance are required, along with annual defensive driving and aviation safety training, as an occupational clearance for ramp delivery and apron access.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Wellington; online portal 'myIR' at www.ird.govt.nz; corporate registration via New Zealand Companies Office (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz) and New Zealand Customs Service (www.customs.govt.nz) for bonded/CCA approvals.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-controlled International Company must: (1) incorporate as a New Zealand company or register as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993, obtaining a NZ Business Number (NZBN); (2) apply for an IRD number using the IR596 form (non-resident company) or online through myIR once a New Zealand registered office and local agent (resident director or authorized representative) are appointed; (3) register for GST (form IR356 or via myIR) where taxable supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in 12 months; (4) apply to the New Zealand Customs Service for a Customs Controlled Area (CCA) licence, an approved cargo/food store warrant, and obtain a Customs client code for duty/GST-suspended importation and export documentation; (5) obtain Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) food premises registration and an aviation catering HACCP certification for the airport kitchen.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation with Territorial_Sourcing for non-residents; a New Zealand-incorporated IC is resident and taxed on worldwide income at 28% corporate rate, while a non-resident (overseas-registered) IC is taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income; the customs-bonded airport kitchen functions as a Tax_Exempt_Zone for indirect tax purposes (GST zero-rating on 'stores' supplied to international flights and duty/GST suspension on imported inputs under the Customs and Excise Act 2018).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box pass-through election exists for companies in New Zealand. The IC may elect 'Look-Through Company' status (LTC) under the Taxation (Annual Rates for 2010-11, Measures No.3) Act 2010 if it has ≤5 owners, all individuals/eligible trusts and meets the 80% test, or use the 'Qualifying Company' regime only for grandfathered cases. Hybrid mismatch elections can be made under the OECD hybrid mismatch rules (Part FM of the Income Tax Act 2007) to elect ordering of rules for MNE structures; GST grouping election under GST Act 1985 ss 55-55B; GST zero-rating of land purchase election (s 11(1)(mb)); no de minimis VAT regrouping in NZ. For meals supplied as ship/stores, election to zero-rate requires the supplier to hold written airline purchase orders confirming the international-flight 'stores' end-use.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, administered by the IRD; customs duty and excise suspended in a Customs Controlled Area under the Customs and Excise Act 2018
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 taxable supplies in the preceding 12 months (mandatory GST registration; voluntary registration available; a non-resident IC supplying zero-rated stores to international aircraft may register even with lower turnover to claim input VAT refunds).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no government-issued fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or real-time tax invoice clearance mandate. E-invoicing is voluntary and uses the Peppol network (TRA, Te Tari Taake requires B2G e-invoices on Peppol from 2025 for public sector contracts); the catering company must issue a valid tax invoice with GST number and, for zero-rated stores, the invoice must state 'zero-rated' (s 24 GST Act) and be archived with the Customs export documentation; Customs SW (CusWeb) JMS is used for export entries, with the CCA operator lodging export declarations in the Customs Electronic System (CES) for each inflight delivery.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under GST Act 1985 s 11(1)(h)/(i) (stores for craft/vessel engaged in international carriage). Meals, beverages, and bonded-inflight food must: (a) be delivered into the aircraft from the CCA kitchen by the IC; (b) be consumed in connection with an international leg (outbound or inbound where the airline is non-resident); (c) be supported by airline purchase orders and flight schedules; and (d) be entered on the Customs electronic manifest/export declaration. Offshore services (e.g., menu R&D charged to the foreign airline head office) may be zero-rated under s 11(2)(c) if supplied to a non-resident who is outside NZ when the services are performed. The IC can also claim refunds of input GST on raw materials via its standard GST return; no statutory FX repatriation deadline applies in NZ law - the 180-day benchmark reflects the airline's standard payment terms and prudential evidence-retention cutoff, and any delayed settlement beyond arm's length may trigger transfer pricing adjustments under s GC 6 Income Tax Act 2007.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CusWeb/Electronic Cargo Transhipment/Customs Export Entry lodged via the Customs Electronic System and the CCA operator's air waybill/ramp delivery manifest)
Bonded Catering transfer records (Stock Status Report of the CCA; duty/GST suspension store records; airline signature of the in-flight catering delivery docket / ULD seal record)
Commercial invoice and zero-rated tax invoice issued per s 24 GST Act 1985 showing 'zero-rated' and the airline's GST status
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 or bank statement evidencing receipt of payment from the foreign airline within the 180-day contractual benchmark
Flight departure documentation (aircraft movement report, flight number/leg confirmation, CTA log) proving the goods left New Zealand on an international service

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) – the integrated financial regulator and central bank, responsible for monetary policy, banking supervision, and the oversight of the NZ dollar wholesale settlement system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is fully convertible. New Zealand has no exchange controls on capital or current account transactions; therefore, non-resident profits and dividends may be repatriated freely, subject to ordinary tax compliance and AML/CFT vetting by the receiving bank. No central bank approval is required for any currency conversion, but companies must transact through an authorised NZ-registered bank or registered financial service provider.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand law imposes no mandatory surrender or compulsory repatriation of export proceeds. Exporters may invoice in foreign currency and retain funds overseas, provided that for New Zealand tax purposes those earnings are declared. Banks handling export settlements require underlying documents (airway bill, commercial invoice, CERS export declaration) and may reject transactions if the remittance does not match the declared trade value.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account, Operational Account and FX Hedging Facility
Operational Account and Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium feasibility for offshore digital EMIs as a primary banking relationship. Offshore EMIs are not licensed banks in New Zealand and cannot access domestic clearing and settlement systems (ESAS). They may act only as secondary payment corridors for expense disbursements and foreign-exchange float, but legal constraints require them to hold an NZ Financial Service Provider (FSP) licence if onboarding NZ-resident customers. The ultimate AML/CFT responsibility remains with the operating company. Hence, no operational treasury concentration should be warehoused with an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: All major NZ banks allow remote onboarding for non-resident companies, provided at least one director or authorised signatory is verified via certified notarised passport copies and a live video call (KYC interview). Physical presence is not statutorily mandated; however, for complex international-company ownership structures or where the bank cannot verify the beneficial owner through public registries, banks may require attendance at a nominated branch or embassy/notary verification session. Recommend naming a locally resident director or secretary to expedite the process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership routed through an offshore trust in a tax-exempt zone.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the trust deed or IC register; waiver or consent from the protector; tax identification number of the settlor/beneficiary; source-of-wealth declaration; bank references from the original jurisdiction; signed declaration confirming compliance with NZ AML/CFT rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Tax-Exempt Zone (International Company) elected structure with no local substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid company registration certificate; registered office/local agent agreement; letters of intent from NZ-based aviation catering buyers; lease or service agreements evidencing operational substance; employment contracts of managerial staff; payroll and office utility documentation; tax opinion letter confirming eligibility and reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpectedly large inbound capital injection relative to initial revenue projection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorising the injection; share subscription agreement or shareholder loan deed; group funding flow diagram; audited financial statements for the parent; business plan with 12-month cash-flow forecast; written confirmation that funds are unencumbered and not derived from prohibited activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan payments should be routed via SWIFT MT103 with purpose code 'EQUI' (equity injection) or 'LOAN' (intercompany lending), and the reference field must quote the share allotment resolution or loan agreement. Prior to the wire, the account officer must receive: (i) certified board resolution; (ii) updated share registry; (iii) source-of-funds statement; (iv) signed KYC questionnaire; (v) tax declaration (IRD number, if applicable). Use the bank's dedicated treasury onboarding team and nominate an account signatory. For large amounts (greater than NZD 1M), pre-clear with the bank's financial-crime unit and obtain a reference number to avoid freezing.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for aviation-catering inputs (raw food, packaging, fuel and equipment) should be made using SWIFT MT103 (individual, itemised remittance) with appropriate purpose codes such as 'TRADE' or 'EQUIP'. For high-value or recurring contracts over NZD 250,000, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit (sight or deferred, UCP 600) is recommended to protect both parties. Local disbursements with NZ-based vendors can settle via BECS direct entry or the faster-payment rails within NZ. Every outgoing payment must include the underlying order/contract number and the beneficiary's full details; otherwise the bank may reject the transaction under its EFTPOS/ACH system controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (plain-vanilla NZD/USD, NZD/CNY and NZD/AUD crosses) for up to 12 months with a registered local bank
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed with approved international counterparties where a physical NZD delivery is impractical
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) for converting NZD floating-rate debt into foreign-currency fixed-rate obligations, with board approval and hedge-alignment documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of date of incorporation; return date determined by the Registrar; filing due within 20 working days after the return date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The company is flagged as 'in default,' loses access to certificates of compliance, and triggers Registrar enforcement; after two consecutive missed annual returns the Registrar may initiate administrative strike-off, dissolving the company under the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements Filing (conditional on audit/filing triggers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after annual balance date (standard 31 March balance date); filing due within 10 working days after the financial statements are completed and signed.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors incur personal liability for default; statutory offence fines up to NZD 50,000 under the Financial Reporting Act 2013, daily penalty for continuing breach, and Registrar capacity to place the company in default leading to deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (submitted through the Company Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same 20-working-day window as the Company Annual Return; any qualifying share transfer or control change must be entered in the UBO register within 10 working days of the relevant event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False or misleading UBO statements are a criminal offence carrying fines and imprisonment exposure for officers; persistent non-maintenance of the UBO register compounds default status and supports strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is compulsory for all FMC reporting entities, and for every 'large' for-profit company in the preceding two consecutive accounting periods — total group assets exceeding NZD 60 million, total annual group revenue exceeding NZD 30 million, or at least 50 full-time-equivalent employees; shareholders holding 5% or more of the voting rights may additionally requisition an audit of a smaller company.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: External Reporting Board (XRB) regime: NZ IFRS (Tier 1) for public-accountability entities; NZ IFRS with Reduced Disclosure Regime (Tier 2) for large and non-public-accountability companies; NZ Simplified Reporting Framework (Tier 3) and Simple Format Reporting (Tier 4) for small and medium owner-managed companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain a physical or electronic register of ultimate beneficial owners at its registered office identifying every individual holding, directly or indirectly, 25% or more of the shares or voting rights, or exercising significant control over the company; any transfer of shares or change of control requires the register to be updated within 10 working days, and the register is annually re-affirmed via the Company Annual Return declaration filed with the New Zealand Companies Office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board and Shareholder meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 – USD 700 per annum (market rate for NZ registered office, company secretarial, and annual return handling services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 15,000 per annum (indicative certified audit fee for a mid-market insured inflight-catering operation, payable only when statutory audit triggers apply)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% on taxable business income attributable to the New Zealand permanent establishment (PE); the Cook Islands International Company (IC) itself is statutorily exempt from Cook Islands income tax under the International Companies Act 2012
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general NZ tax holidays. Effective reliefs relevant to an inbound non-resident IC: (1) zero-rating under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for exported in-flight meals and services supplied to international airlines (0% GST); (2) the 15% Research & Development Tax Incentive credit if the catering kitchen performs eligible R&D; (3) the Approved Issuer Levy at 2% in lieu of 15% NRWT on qualifying interest; (4) the Foreign Investor Tax Credit (FITC)/supplementary dividend regime offsetting NZ NRWT on non-resident shareholders; (5) the Cook Islands IC's home-jurisdiction exemption means non-NZ-source income of the IC is not subject to NZ tax provided the place of effective management remains outside NZ
